column1: # Old Turkic for the "Write in ..." tool (scribe.js); built into scribe-langs.js by scripts/make-scribe.ps1.
# The Orkhon runic script, written from right to left. Values follow Tekin (A Grammar of Orkhon Turkic, 1968): ¹ marks a
# consonant used with back vowels (a ı o u), ² one used with front vowels (e i ö ü). The keys type one exact sign; typed
# words are spelt by the rules in scribe.js (turkicWord): the consonants take the form of the word's vowels; a and e are
# written only at the end of a word (or in a word of one syllable), ı/i always, o/u and ö/ü in the first syllable; q next
# to o/u is the sign oq, k after an unwritten ö/ü the sign ök; nt, lt, nč, ny and ŋ have signs of their own.

column4: Old Turkic was carved in a runic script of its own, read from right to left, on the memorial stones of the Turkic khagans in Mongolia (720s–730s) and on rocks and objects from the Yenisei to the Danube.

column2: The runes of the Orkhon inscriptions, raised for Kül Tigin (732) and Bilge Kagan (735) by the Orkhon river in Mongolia, the oldest long texts in a Turkic language.

Type Turkic words as they sound (Tekin’s spelling: ı, ö, ü, q, ɣ or ğ, š, č, ŋ or ng): each consonant takes its back or front form from the word’s vowels, and the vowels are written as on the stones. The keys add one exact sign, back (¹) or front (²). Spaces become the two dots between words.
